# `.github/workflows`

The workflows, which the root's Workflow describes as rules.

The rules across the game are the [root AGENTS.md](../../AGENTS.md).

- `branch-policy.yml`: fails a PR whose branch holds a merge commit (PR branches are linear).
- `pr-preview-build.yml`: builds a PR's preview with a read-only token (the lab's and the preview scripts' unit tests, the typecheck and build, the Pages paths), forks included.
- `pr-preview.yml`: a `workflow_run`, always the copy on `main`, which checks the artifact's PR number against the API and publishes it in the aggregated `gh-pages` branch. **Never run PR code in it.** It holds no code of its own: each step calls a module of [`scripts/preview`](../../scripts/preview/AGENTS.md), checked out from the run's own commit (main's head) and unit-tested (`npm run preview:test`). Each build has a folder of its own, `pr-preview/pr-N/<sha7>/`, which the comment links (#299): Pages' CDN caches a path for up to 10 minutes, 404s included, and ignores a query string, so a build published over the last at one path was served old for minutes after the comment said ready. A commit's folder is a path nothing asked for before it's served, and it's called ready only once probe files published with it are served (a 404 the CDN caches lands on a probe). `pr-preview/pr-N/` is the stable page (`.github/preview-index.html`, main's copy), which goes to the newest build by the PR's `latest.json` (building, ready or failed), read from the branch through GitHub's API, never the CDN: while a push builds it says how long, the previous build linked as such (#292). The newest three folders are kept, so a stable page served from the cache never goes to one that's gone; a folder pruned, or a closed PR's preview, is answered by production's `404.html`, which sends it to the PR's stable page or the game (an installed app left there showed Pages' plain 404: `scripts/AGENTS.md`). The build itself (`pr-preview-build.yml`) makes the folder: `--base` ends in the commit's seven characters, and a stable page is put beside it, so main's copy before #299, which published the whole artifact at `pr-N/`, publishes it right too. Every job that writes `gh-pages` or deploys Pages, production's included, is in the `pages-publisher` group: GitHub keeps one pending job a group, so a third arriving cancels the pending one, and a publish was lost when several PRs' builds finished at once (#329's on 2026-10-31: its comment stood at "building" until it was re-run by hand).
- **So every publish catches up the others** (`pr-preview.yml`'s publish job): holding the group, it publishes its own build and, for every open PR whose `latest.json` doesn't record its head as ready or failed (nor, built before #299, its root's `preview-metadata.json`), that head's newest finished build, its artifact downloaded (`gh run download`, plain files only) and its `pr.json` checked against the API as its own is; a preview whose PR was closed unmerged is removed. All of them go in one push, one deploy and one probe each, and each PR's sticky comment is written by the job itself (the marker `marocchino/sticky-pull-request-comment` uses, so the building job's comment is the same one). It runs for every finished build, cancelled and skipped ones too, and after every production deploy (a `workflow_run` of `Deploy GitHub Pages`), so whichever job holds the group last is a publish, and it sees every build that finished before it: a build's publish can still be cancelled, never lost. A build a catch-up published is skipped when its own run comes (its run's URL is in `latest.json`). Run the workflow by hand (`gh workflow run pr-preview.yml`) to catch up without a build; `--ref` a branch runs that branch's copy, which is how a change to it is tried before it's merged. Dropping the group for the publish and retrying the push wasn't enough: each publish deploys the whole branch as it checked it out, so two at once could deploy a snapshot without the other's build.
- **Where Pages serves the site is its settings', read as the publish starts** (`pr-preview.yml`'s publish, `siteOrigin` in
  `scripts/preview/steps.mjs`: the Pages API's `html_url`, or the `SITE_ORIGIN` variable if set): the game has its own domain, `last-stand.cc`, since
  2026-10-31, and the github.io address answers every path with a redirect there. Built from the github.io address,
  the probes read the redirect's page, and every publish failed after 60 s though its build was served. The probes
  follow a redirect too. The build reads the same (`pr-preview-build.yml`, with `pages: read`) for its base path,
  none on the domain's root: built under `/last-stand/`, a preview on last-stand.cc asked for every file at a path
  that isn't there and stood on its loading screen. `404.html` takes a path as a project site's only where its
  second part is `pr-preview`. Pages must enforce HTTPS: over plain http a page has no WebGPU, service worker or install.
- `deploy-pages.yml`: on a merge to `main`, production at the root of `gh-pages`, the open PRs' previews kept.

Don't switch Pages to "GitHub Actions only", and don't delete the `gh-pages` branch.
